summary: Sam Bankman-Fried (Samuel Benjamin Bankman-Fried, born March 5, 1992) was convicted on seven counts of fraud and related offenses in the Southern District of New York, sentenced to 25 years imprisonment on March 28, 2024 by Judge Lewis Kaplan, and is currently incarcerated at MDC Brooklyn under inmate number 37244-510. He is pursuing an appeal before the Second Circuit, which remains unresolved, and federal investigators have alleged he stole $35 million from Alameda Research customer accounts. No final civil judgments or sanctions beyond these allegations have been located, and the BOP has not published a projected release date for his inmate number, leaving only third‑party estimates available.

findings.statement: Sam Bankman-Fried's full legal name is Samuel Benjamin Bankman-Fried and his date of birth is March 5, 1992.
Sam Bankman-Fried was convicted of all seven counts and sentenced to 25 years in prison on March 28, 2024 by Judge Lewis Kaplan in the Southern District of New York.
Sam Bankman-Fried is pursuing an appeal while incarcerated; no appellate ruling has been reported yet.
After conviction and sentencing, Sam Bankman-Fried was assigned federal inmate register number 37244-510 and is incarcerated at MDC Brooklyn.
According to a Yahoo News report, the BOP estimates that Sam Bankman-Fried will be released on December 14, 2044.
The political action committee associated with his brother came under federal scrutiny after it was discovered that Sam had stolen $35 million from Alameda Research customer accounts.
As of the latest available information, Sam Bankman-Fried's appeal is pending before the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit, with no decision rendered.
The Bureau of Prisons inmate locator does not publicly display a projected release date for register 37244-510; external sources estimate a release around December 2044.

gaps: The exact projected release date as shown in the official BOP inmate locator for register 37244-510 has not been located in the evidence; only third‑party estimates are available.
No final civil judgment or regulatory sanction beyond the alleged Alameda theft has been identified in public court or regulatory databases.
The outcome of the appeal before the Second Circuit remains unknown; no appellate decision has been published.
